courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: So this authentication form is of course managed in the auth page and there thus far,
I have my ion-list with my e-mail in there, my e-mail input.
I will actually keep that e-mail input there but that is of course not all I want,
I also want a second ion-item and remember, you should wrap your labels and inputs in ion-items to get
some extra styling and behavior, like that floating label,
it will also be important for validation and correctly showing when there is an error in the input.
So definitely use an ion-item here and then I'll add another ion-label where I say password and that label
should also have a position of floating and below that ,we can use or we can add our ion-input which should
be of type password.
Now the first one doesn't have a type,
we could set one to text but that is the default anyways.
So now we have a password input and we have a text input, that is pretty nice,
now I also want an extra button that allows me to toggle between sign-up and sign-in mode,
so between logging in and signing up and therefore, I'll add another button here where I say switch
to login,
though we will set this text dynamically soon because of course that should say switch to sign-up
if we're in login mode already and there I'll use a color of primary
but I'll set the fill mode to clear which basically make sure that we only have the text and nothing
else.
Now if we save that and we let this page reload, this is what we get, not too bad but also not entirely
what I want,
I also want the buttons to be beneath each other and not sit next to each other as they do here
and of course, there are various ways of achieving that.
We can simply wrap then into divs for example,
you could also manually style them via CSS and turn them to block buttons or here we can actually
take advantage of another attribute Ionic allows us to set on an ion-button and that's the expand attribute
and you can set this to block or to full. Now if you set this to full, this takes the entire line and
the difference between block and full becomes pretty clear
once I do the same on the other button. If I set this to full,
you see now it looks like this
and if I set this to block,
it looks the same, right.
Not entirely, one difference you'll note is the corners. With block, we have rounded corners here
as you can see and if I switch this back to full, you will see we have no rounded corners. Now the rounded corners
are not the only difference, it becomes clearer if I go to my second button here and I give this a fill
of, not of clear, but of outline, to make sure that this is a button without a background color but with a
border and you see for full, there is no left to right border because the idea behind full is that it
takes the full width of the container.
Now here, we just happened to have some padding set on our content which is why this button doesn't take
the full page width but if you would have this in some other container that does take the full page
width, then with expand full, you take that full width, with expand block on the other hand,
you also take that full width but you leave a little bit of spacing on the left or right and you keep
your left and right borders.
So this just is a button that takes the full width but looks like a normal button otherwise, full is a
special button that takes the full width and is also styled to be a seamless button going from left
to right without clear borders you could say. Now I'll remove fill outline here but I'll keep expand
block here and I'll also set expand block on the first button and therefore we now have two buttons
that simply take the full entire width of their parent container and therefore they are now positioned
beneath each other.
Now I also will wrap that in a grid here, so I'll add ion-grid with ion-row and ion-col because
I want to control my sizes and I'll set a size on a medium sized or bigger screens of 6 and an offset-md
of three therefore to center this and in that column, I'll add this list here and then I'll
add another row below that with another column with the same rules,
so therefore we can of course just copy them if you want, like that
and in this column, I'll have my two buttons here, like that.
And now with that, we should have the same look here on the mobile device,
that shouldn't change but on bigger screens as I expand this, this doesn't take the full screen size
and maybe we can even start at small screens
now that I think about this,
so let me change this to size-sm and offset-sm on both ion-columns here, so that we actually already
take less width on smaller screens like this one because there, I think it's also enough if it's
centered in the middle.
Yes, that should be OK
and on mobile devices, it still looks the way it did.
So these are the visuals,
that is how our form looks like. Now it's time to also make sure it works like a form.
